in_arabic.name: أُسْمَانِيٌ
in_arabic.long_meaning: أُسْمَانِيٌ: مُتَبَصِرٌ، عَصَبي، مُتَفَوق، جَذَبٌ، مُتَأَجِّد، يَتميّز بِعِزٍّ، وَيُحسِنُ إقامة الحُدوقِ، وَيَنال العُلا، وَيُذَكِّي بِالتَوديعِ، وَيَزال مُتَمَنِّعاً، وَيُبَلِّغُ العُمرَ، وَيُقَرِّبُ المَنَّةَ، وَيُحفَظُ، وَيُكَفِّلُ، وَيُحسِنُ الإِرثَ، وَيُبَلِّغُ الحُضورَ، وَيُطَوِّلُ النَظَرَ، وَيُجَرِّبُ الأَمورَ، وَيُجَرِّبُ الأَسلوبَ، وَيُبَلِّغُ المَعروفَ، وَيُشَكِّلُ الحُكمةَ، وَيُؤَيَّدُ، وَيُؤَجِّلُ، وَيُقَرِّبُ الرَأيَ، وَيُحسِنُ الحُججَ

data.cultural_impact: Usmani is a prominent surname in the Muslim world, particularly in South Asia. The name derives from Osman, the legendary founder of the Ottoman Empire in the late 13th century. The name represents a rich and complex historical legacy, rooted in the Islamic Golden Age. As a surname, Usmani signifies pride and connection to this esteemed cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Usmani holds significant spiritual meaning for Muslims, as Osman is considered to be a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). According to Islamic tradition, Usman played a crucial role in the protection and preservation of the Prophet's teachings and the early Islamic community. Thus, the name Usmani is a reminder of the importance of upholding the Quran, Prophetic traditions, and Islamic values in one's life. Additionally, the name is often associated with courage, resilience, and leadership, qualities that are highly valued in Islamic belief.
